verdicts.why: In A.K.A. Everything Jessica tells Erik she knows he is a good guy but can't trust him, and Costa then approaches him at the bar saying Jessica recommended him. The romance ends there and has no stage.

In S3#6 Erik wakes to find Trish at his bedside, recognizes her voice, says she has saved him twice and promises to keep her secret. That is where he first knows who she is, before the S3#10 stage. In S3#4 she was a masked stranger to him.

In Revelations Matt confronts Lantom for hiding that Maggie is his mother and walks away, 'seemingly destroying his relationship with Murdock for good'. That is a clear falling-out with no stage before Lantom's death in S3#10.

In A New Napkin Daredevil hangs Manning from a roof, and Manning offers to testify that Vanessa ordered Nadeem's death and Fisk ordered Winn's and Julie Barnes's. The fixer turning on his boss is a clear betrayal with no stage.
The Punisher kills Grotto in S2#3, and in Penny and Dime Lantom holds his funeral, which only Matt, Foggy and Karen attend. A death is a stage, and S2#4 is not earlier than either event.

Both events are real: Karen tells Foggy she killed Wesley in S3#5 and he reassures her in S3#6, and in S3#13 Foggy proposes Nelson, Murdock & Page. But an added stage has to start in the episode where its events happen, so a stage at S3#13 can only tell the partnership.

value.title: Daredevil S3#13
value.text: Once Fisk is back in prison, Foggy asks Karen to join him and Matt as partners in a new firm, Nelson, Murdock & Page.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Close friend from her first day at the firm. Becomes Foggy's law partner.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Close friend who makes Karen a partner in Nelson, Murdock & Page.

verdicts.why: In Heaven's Half Hour, Matt, Foggy and Karen are celebrating at Josie's when Dex kills Foggy. A death is a stage, and this connection has none for it.
In World on Fire Foggy goes to Landman and Zack and faces Marci, his ex, over Elena Cardenas's case. Their connection starts there, long before The Defenders.
They sleep together in S1#11, and in S1#12 Foggy convinces Marci to help and she starts sending him Landman and Zack documents on Fisk. Here the rivalry clearly turns into an alliance.
Seven Minutes in Heaven: 'Nelson and Murdock agree to part ways'. That is a clear falling-out with no stage.
In S3#12 they work together as lawyers again, and in S3#13 Foggy suggests they start Nelson, Murdock & Page. This clear reconciliation after the S2 split has no stage.

In The Man in the Box, Reyes has Nelson, Murdock and Page meet her, admits her office ran the sting behind the Castle massacre and pleads for help, then is gunned down in front of them, and Foggy is wounded. A death is a stage.

The fight is real (Theo blames Foggy in S3#11) and so is the rescue (in S3#13 Foggy gets Tower to go after Red Lion, and Theo is free if he repays the loan). But a stage at S3#13 should only tell what happens there.

value.title: Daredevil S3#13
value.text: Foggy gets the Red Lion bank taken down, and Theo stays free of charges as long as he pays back the fraudulent loan. Theo thanks his brother for saving him.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Foggy's younger brother, whom Foggy keeps out of prison.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Theo's older brother, who keeps him out of prison.

verdicts.why: In S5#11 Piper's secret deal with Hale leads the team into the trap. She holds them at gunpoint, Ruby cuts off Yo-Yo's arms, and Piper sits alone with her part in it, then is jailed in S5#12. A betrayal with these consequences is a clear turn. The kind stays friend, since they later serve on the same team.

value.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S5#11
value.text: Piper's secret deal with General Hale leads the team into an ambush, where Ruby cuts off Yo-Yo's arms. Piper blames herself.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Teammate whose deal with Hale leads to the ambush that costs Yo-Yo her arms.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Friend who loses her arms in the ambush Piper's deal leads to.

verdicts.why: In Straight to Hell Castle waits in Matt's apartment because Karen asked him to protect Matt. They fight off the AVTF together and argue over killing North. This new alliance has no stage.
In Virtue of the Vicious Wilson takes Karen hostage with a dead man's switch. Castle helps her get free and lets Wilson blow himself up. His death has no stage.

In S3#12 Sallinger laces Jessica's drink, ties her up in her office and photographs her for a 'confession'. Her hidden camera records him admitting to Dorothy's murder, and she leaves him for the police. He never kidnaps her, so the current text is wrong.

They never share a title. Paradise Lost has only James's line that he assumed Jiaying would send Gordon. That Gordon brought him into Afterlife comes from the fandom bio and is not shown in the episode's own summary. Knowing about someone's role is not a connection.

The coercion is real, but it starts in Closure (S3#9): Giyera tortures Simmons so Ward can make Fitz explain the portal, and Fitz agrees to guide the Hydra team through it. The stage belongs at S3#9, and its text should only tell what happens there.

value.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3#9
value.text: Ward has Jemma tortured to make Fitz explain the portal, and Fitz agrees to guide Ward's Hydra team through it.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Former friend Ward drops into the ocean, and later forces to guide him through the portal.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Hydra traitor who drops Fitz into the ocean, and later forces him through the portal.

verdicts.why: The session where the Fisks talk through Vanessa's affair with Adam is in Sic Semper Systema (S1#4). In S1#3 Heather only appears at Matt's apartment.
The scene is real: in S2#7 Fisk confides in Heather and gives her the matching earring. But nothing turns. She already serves his administration, and one moment of confiding is not a clear turn.

At Karen's trial Heather gives the prosecution her assessment of Karen. Matt objects, then asks whether she is hiding behind Fisk's administration. The exes now face each other as opponents, which is a clear turn after the S2#2 breakup.

In S2#2 and S2#3 Vanessa draws Heather into the Fisks' circle. Vanessa dies in S2#5, and in S2#6 Heather mourns before her photo at the reception and pockets one of her red earrings. A death is a stage.

In S1#3 Hector is stunned and feels betrayed when Matt outs him. He is acquitted, ignores Matt's warning to stop, and is shot dead that night. He never learns Matt is Daredevil, so 'respect each other as fellow vigilantes' is wrong.

In S1#3 Hector tells Soledad from the stand that he has bought them a new place, and they leave court together after the verdict. He is killed that night, leaving her a widow. The current text leaves out his death, which is the main event between them in this title.

In S3#18 Radcliffe throws Fitz and Jemma out, and Fitz pleads for his help against Hive before Daisy and Alisha take Radcliffe away. They work together after S3#22. The connection starts in S3, not S4#1.
In S1#10 at Niku, Hope stabs herself in the neck so Jessica no longer has to keep Kilgrave alive, and as she dies she makes Jessica promise to kill him. A death is a stage.

They never meet. Hartley only hears from Bobbi of Fury's secret order to scuttle the Iliad, and Fury's involvement has no huge personal consequence for her. Knowing about the director is not a connection.
The only shared scene (S1#8) is Wesley reporting to Fisk and Owlsley at Melvin's workshop, with nothing passing between Wesley and Melvin. Being in the same room is not a connection.

In Speak of the Devil (S1#9) Nobu threatens to rip out Wesley's tongue for mistranslating him. Wesley and Fisk set Nobu against the masked man and stand over his burning body. The alliance turns hostile and ends in his death, with no stage.
In S1#9 Jeri, alone with the captive Kilgrave, agrees to his idea of stopping Wendy and cuts the wires. The connection starts there, before the S1#10 stage where he takes control of her.
Jeri's cut wire keeps Jessica from stopping Louise's death in S1#9. In S1#10 Jessica arrives at Wendy's house and confronts Jeri over her part in it. The betrayal has no stage.
In S3#13 Jeri shoots Jessica in the leg when she rushes her, and leaves with Trish. She arranges Trish's escape, then calls Jessica once Trish is locked in the shipping coffin.
In S3#13 Kith thanks Jeri but says goodbye, saying Jeri only did it because of a danger she created herself. 'Kith breaks things off with Hogarth.' The end of the romance has no stage.

The real Ward is dead by S3 and is not plugged into the Framework. Mace only meets a Framework program of Ward, and a Framework version is not the person. They never share a title, so nothing is left to connect them.

In AKA Freak Accident (S2#2) Jessica comes to believe Simpson was only protecting Trish. When Alisa attacks he tells Jessica to take Trish and run, she unties him, and he is killed. A clear turn and a death, with no stage.

Jessica spots Malus at the aquarium in S2#5, and in S2#6 she tracks him to his home, where she finds him living with the woman who claims to be her mother. The connection starts well before the only stage at S2#11.

In Mean Right Hook (Defenders #2) Misty catches Jessica taking evidence at Raymond's hideout, arrests her outside her building and interrogates her until Matt arrives as her lawyer. That is where they meet, before #7.
